data.name: Vitaline
data.gender_notes: Vitaline is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'vitalis', meaning 'life-giving'. In Christian tradition, it can be interpreted as a name for someone who embodies the vibrancy and vitality of life. The name Vitaline carries the meaning “Life-giving, vibrant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Vitaline usually hope their child will grow to embody life-giving, vibrant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the life-giving spirit of God
data.etymology: Vitaline belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Life-giving, vibrant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vitaline total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: ויטאלין
in_hebrew.meaning: השם ויטאלין נגזר מלטינית ומשמעותו חיים או קשור לחיים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ויטאלין מקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'של חיים' או 'קשור לחיים'. הוא קשור למילה הלטינית 'vitalis', שפירושה 'של חיים' או 'חיוני'. השם ויטאלין משקף את החשיבות של החיים ואת הקשר שלהם לאלוהים ולרוחניות בנצרות.

in_greek.name: Βιταλίνη
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Βιταλίνη προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Vitalis και σημαίνει ζωή ή που σχετίζεται με τη ζωή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βιταλίνη έχει τις ρίζες του στο λατινικό όνομα Vitalis, που σημαίνει 'της ζωής' ή 'που σχετίζεται με τη ζωή'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η έννοια της ζωής συνδέεται συχνά με την πνευματική ζωή και τη σχέση με τον Θεό. Το όνομα Βιταλίνη αντανακλά την πνευματική σημασία της ζωής και την αναζήτηση της αιώνιας ζωής μέσω της πίστης.

in_latin.name: Vitaline
in_latin.meaning: The name Vitaline derives from Latin and means 'of life' or 'related to life'
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Vitaline originates from the Latin name Vitalis, meaning 'of life' or 'vital'. The name Vitaline reflects the importance of life and its connection to God and spirituality in Christianity.

data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Vitaline can be seen as a reminder of the inherent value and potential for life. It is a name that encourages one to embrace the gifts of life with gratitude and zest, while also recognizing the Divine Source of that life. The name invites us to live our lives in a way that reflects the love, joy, and light that comes from our relationship with God. In essence, Vitaline is a name that encourages us to live life to the fullest, embracing each moment as a gift from God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vitaline signifies the essence of vitality and divine life within us. It is a reminder of God's revitalizing and rejuvenating power, inspiring us to live fully and faithfully in His presence.

historical_references.reference: Vitalis of Milana, also known as Vitalis the Martyr, was an early Christian bishop and martyr of the late 3rd or early 4th century. He is believed to have been a bishop in Milan, Italy, and was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Diocletian. According to legend, Vitalis was arrested, interrogated, and tortured, but remained steadfast in his faith and was eventually beheaded.
historical_references.context: Early Christianity, Persecutions of Emperor Diocletian

historical_references.reference: Vitalis of Savona, also known as Saint Vitalis, was a bishop and martyr of the 5th century. He is believed to have been the bishop of Savona, Italy, and was martyred during the Vandal invasions of Italy. According to legend, Vitalis was arrested and interrogated by the Vandals, who demanded that he renounce Christianity. When he refused, he was tortured and then beheaded.
historical_references.context: Late Antiquity, Vandal invasions of Italy
